slides.title: Welcome to HTML Tables
slides.content:
# HTML Tables: Structuring Data 📊

Tables represent two-dimensional tabular data arranged in rows and columns.

## What you'll master:
- 🧱 **Table Building Blocks** - `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<td>`, and `<th>`
- 🧠 **Semantic Sectioning** - `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, and `<tfoot>`
- 📑 **Table Metadata** - `<caption>` and accessibility headers with `scope`
- 🔀 **Merging Cells** - `colspan` (columns) and `rowspan` (rows)
- 🎨 **Table Styling & Responsive Patterns** - Zebra striping, borders, and overflow wrapping

slides.title: Core Table Elements
slides.content:
# Core Table Elements 🧱 An HTML table is constructed using four fundamental tags: 1. ``: The outer wrapper that defines the table. 2. ``: **Table Row** — defines a horizontal row of cells. 3. `
`: **Table Header** — contains bold, centered header titles. 4. ``: **Table Data** — contains regular data cells. ```html_not
Fruit Color
Apple Red
Banana Yellow
```

slides.title: Semantic Grouping: thead, tbody, tfoot
slides.content:
# Semantic Grouping: thead, tbody, tfoot 🏛️ To make tables accessible and structured, split content into three distinct semantic sections: ```html_not
Product Qty Price
Wireless Mouse 2 $40.00
Mechanical Keyboard 1 $90.00
Total 3 $130.00
```

slides.title: The <caption> Element
slides.content:
# Table Captions (``) 🏷️ The `` element provides a title or description for the entire table. ```html_not
Quarterly Sales Performance (2025)
Quarter Revenue
Q1 $120,000
``` ## Important Rules: - The `` tag **must** be placed immediately following the opening `` tag! - It is automatically centered above the table by default.

slides.title: Header Scope Attribute
slides.content:
# Header Accessibility with `scope` 👓 The `scope` attribute on `` elements explicitly tells screen readers whether the header applies to a column or a row. ```html_not
Employee Department Salary
Alice Chen Engineering $110,000
Bob Smith Design $95,000
``` ## Scope Values: - `scope="col"`: Header for a column. - `scope="row"`: Header for a row. - `scope="colgroup"` / `scope="rowgroup"`: Header for multi-column or multi-row groups.

slides.title: Merging Columns with colspan
slides.content:
# Merging Columns with `colspan` ➡️ The `colspan` attribute merges two or more adjacent columns into a single cell. ```html_not
Full Name Role
John Doe Developer
``` ## Notice: Because the header cell has `colspan="2"`, it spans across two columns, matching the two `` cells (John, Doe) in the row below it!

slides.title: Merging Rows with rowspan
slides.content:
# Merging Rows with `rowspan` ⬇️ The `rowspan` attribute merges two or more vertical rows into a single cell. ```html_not
Category Item Price
Electronics Phone $699
Laptop $1,199
``` ## How It Works: The cell with `rowspan="2"` pushes down into the next row. The second row only needs two `` elements because the first column is already occupied!

slides.title: Complex Layouts: Combining Colspan & Rowspan
slides.content:
# Combining `colspan` and `rowspan` 🧩 Complex schedules and invoices frequently combine horizontal and vertical spans: ```html_not
Student Exams Final Grade
Midterm Final
Sarah Connor 92 95 A
```

slides.title: Responsive Card Pattern
Table Accessibility (ARIA & Roles)
slides.content:
# Table Accessibility Best Practices ♿

To ensure screen reader compatibility:
- Always use `<th>` for headers, never styled `<td>` elements.
- Always provide `scope="col"` or `scope="row"` on headers.
- Include a descriptive `<caption>`.
- Avoid deeply nested tables for visual layout (use CSS Grid or Flexbox instead!).
- For data with abbreviations, use `<abbr title="Average">Avg</abbr>`.

slides.title: Table Layout: Auto vs Fixed
slides.content:
# Performance: `table-layout: fixed` ⚡

By default, browsers use `table-layout: auto`, inspecting the content of every single cell before deciding column widths. For massive datasets, this causes layout thrashing.

```css_not
table {
  width: 100%;
  table-layout: fixed; /* Super fast rendering! */
}
```

## Advantages of `table-layout: fixed`:
1. **Speed:** Browser only inspects the first row and immediately renders the table.
2. **Predictable Widths:** Column widths strictly respect set percentages.
3. **Ellipsis Truncation:** Allows text truncation with `text-overflow: ellipsis` on table cells!

slides.title: Common Table Pitfalls
slides.content:
# Common Table Pitfalls to Avoid ⚠️

1. ❌ **Using Tables for Page Layout:** Never use tables for general page layout. Tables are strictly for tabular data! Use Flexbox/Grid for layouts.
2. ❌ **Mismatched Column Counts:** When using `colspan` or `rowspan`, forgetting to remove excess cells in subsequent rows distorts the grid.
3. ❌ **Missing Caption/Headings:** Leaves screen readers lost with no context.
4. ❌ **Unstyled Default Borders:** Looks unpolished and amateurish without `border-collapse`.

slides.content:

Grand Total: $7,250.00

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Table Mastery Complete! 🏆

You have mastered structuring tabular datasets with modern standards!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Anatomy:** `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>`.
- ✅ **Semantics:** Group with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, and `<tfoot>`.
- ✅ **Cell Merging:** `colspan` merges horizontally; `rowspan` merges vertically.
- ✅ **Accessibility:** Always include `<caption>` and `scope="col|row"`.
- ✅ **CSS Polish:** Apply `border-collapse: collapse` and zebra striping.
